claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in Southwest Finland wellbeing services county was 1.6% above the national level (ratio 1.016, 95% interval 0.992-1.041), about 19.3 more deaths a year than its age structure predicts.

Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants: Southwest Finland wellbeing services county is at 54.83 (three-year mean to 2025) against 36 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where Southwest Finland wellbeing services county is clearly worse than the country is referral into specialist care.

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: the same fast lane in public primary care that occupational care already gives. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 39.9 deaths a year in Southwest Finland wellbeing services county (range 5-78.6) for an assumed EUR 1,493,400 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 32% of sensitivity runs.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 75.0% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 60% of the gap.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 76.3% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-3.67 percentage points, closing about 82% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
